adequacy_checks.all_must_pass: If any check fails, the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE. INCONCLUSIVE is a terminal outcome for this protocol version; it is not retried by silent adjustment. A revised protocol is a new frozen record with the reason for revision stated.

competing_modes.criterion: The selected f1 peak must exceed the highest competing peak in the search band (outside the main lobe, main lobe defined as +-2 raw bins around the selected peak) by a factor >= 10 in magnitude.
competing_modes.rationale: Rules out contamination by higher bending modes, torsional modes, or numerical artifacts masquerading as f1.

frequency_resolution.criterion: Raw FFT bin width df = 1/T_window <= 0.5 Hz. Interpolated peak accuracy (Hann + 8x zero-pad + parabolic interpolation) must be <= 0.1 Hz, i.e. < 6% of the half-tolerance band.
frequency_resolution.rationale: The estimator's discretization uncertainty must be a small fraction of the acceptance band.

signal_strength.criterion: (a) Peak ringdown amplitude (first 5 cycles after t_settle) >= 100x the RMS of the signal in a quiet band (200-400 Hz) of the same spectrum. (b) RMS amplitude in the last 10% of the window >= 1% of RMS in the first 10% (signal not decayed into numerical noise).
signal_strength.rationale: Adequate SNR throughout the window; guards against over-interpreting a decayed-to-noise tail.

stability_across_windows.criterion: Split the ringdown window into first and second halves; independent f1 estimates from each half must agree within 0.5% (relative).
stability_across_windows.rationale: A stationary modal frequency must be window-independent; disagreement indicates non-stationarity, beating between close modes, or excessive decay.

estimator.name: Hann-windowed FFT peak estimator with parabolic refinement

peak_selection.band_note: [0.7, 1.3] x f_ref. f2 (cantilever) = 6.267 x f1 ~ 255 Hz, well outside the band.
peak_selection.refinement: Parabolic interpolation on the log-magnitude using the peak bin and its two neighbors, after 8x zero-padding.
peak_selection.rule: Highest magnitude peak in the search band. Record peak prominence (ratio to second-highest peak outside the main lobe) and the interpolated frequency.
peak_selection.tie_or_ambiguity: If two peaks in the band are within a factor of 2 in magnitude, the competing-modes adequacy check governs (likely INCONCLUSIVE). No analyst discretion to prefer the peak nearer the reference.

preprocessing.detrend: Remove the mean of the windowed segment (ringdown oscillates about zero after full unload).
steps: Extract face-averaged tip DZ over the ringdown window.
Exclude [t_release, t_release + t_settle] to avoid the release transient.
preprocessing.t_settle_note: ~3 cycles at f1; excludes the broadband release transient while preserving ~78 cycles for the estimate.

excitation.method: Step-unload from the quasi-static 1000 N state. Load ramps 0 -> 1000 N over [0, 0.1] s (same /FUNCT/1 as the static verification), holds to t_release, then ramps to zero over [t_release, t_release + 0.001] s.
excitation.t_ramp_release_note: Fast but non-instantaneous release; avoids exciting non-physical ultra-high-frequency content from a true step.
excitation.t_release_verified_definition: The verified excitation end time is the last timestamp at which face-averaged tip DZ is within 1% of the static hold mean (computed over [0.3, 0.5] s) before the onset of oscillation. It must agree with the deck-specified t_release = 0.5 s within 5 ms (10 output samples); otherwise the outcome is INCONCLUSIVE (actuation did not occur as specified). This is the dynamic analogue of the static campaign's actuation-verification rule.

formulation.note: Identical to the verified static formulation; the dynamic gate tests the mass/stiffness distribution, not a new formulation.

mesh: fine (40x8x8, 2560 bricks) — the verified mesh from the static campaign.

outcome_definitions.FAIL: All adequacy checks pass and |f_est - f_ref| / f_ref > 0.02.
outcome_definitions.INCONCLUSIVE: Any adequacy check fails, or the verified excitation end time disagrees with the deck specification. Terminal for this protocol version.
outcome_definitions.PASS: All adequacy checks pass and |f_est - f_ref| / f_ref <= 0.02.

assumptions: Uniform cross-section, linear elastic, small deflections.
Ideal clamped boundary (all DOFs fixed at wall).
No damping in the analytical model.
Material: E = 200 GPa, rho = 7850 kg/m^3; geometry L = 1.0 m, 0.05 x 0.05 m section.
reference.shear_correction_note: Timoshenko shear correction is 0.195% of bending deflection at L/h = 20; Euler-Bernoulli is an adequate reference.
reference.systematic_offset_note: The 3D solid model includes shear flexibility and 3D clamp effects absent from the EB idealization; a small systematic offset (expected < ~1.5% combined with discretization) is accommodated by the tolerance, not corrected for.

sampling.note: 2 kHz sampling gives ~49 points per f1 cycle; adequate for the 28.5-53 Hz search band with margin against aliasing of low-order modes.
sampling.ringdown_window_note: From t_release + t_settle to t_end: 1.925 s, ~78 cycles at f1. Raw df = 0.52 Hz; meets the <= 0.5 Hz adequacy bound within rounding (0.52 vs 0.50 — see tolerance note).

status: FROZEN — pending review. No run launched under this protocol.

tolerance.rationale: Consistent with the static gate (±2% on fine-mesh deflection). FE frequency error scales ~1/2 the static deflection error for the same mesh (f ~ sqrt(k)); with e_fine = 1.71% static, discretization contributes ~0.85%, leaving margin for 3D/clamp idealization offset. Tight enough to discriminate a wrong mass or stiffness distribution; loose enough not to punish the EB-vs-3D idealization gap.

tolerance_note_on_df: Raw df = 1/1.925 = 0.519 Hz marginally exceeds the 0.5 Hz adequacy bound as stated. The bound is on the raw bin width before interpolation; interpolated accuracy (~0.05 Hz) is what enters the error budget, and 0.519 Hz raw is accepted under this protocol with the rationale recorded here. A stricter reading would extend t_end; that change requires a protocol revision, not a silent edit.
